story_text.value:
Hi HN, I'm Stephan.

I'm an ex-CTO and many companies I look in today, want to get AI coded apps into production, but engineering code reviews are the new bottleneck - and engineers don't even love to do them.

No more code reviews. Fuzz instead.

appfuzz works with WASM and runs the .wasm thousands of times against a simulated backend and reports problems: crashes, n+1 queries, XSS, SQL injection, leaked secrets, blown IO/CPU/instruction budgets.

Try it of your own - you don't need an app for the demo:

https://appfuzz.dev

Why: agents write code faster than anyone can review it, and in many companies people outside engineering (marketing, sales, support) want to ship apps too - pressure from the CEO is high.

But then engineers get the pager alerts.

One way to make them safer is to treat them like iPhone/iOS apps: sandbox, permissions, app review (what appfuzz does).

It works with Wasm components in any language, Spin, wasmCloud, Fastly Compute, and Shopify Functions.

MIT. Very early state.

Which platform should I add, and what should it look for?

https://appfuzz.dev

title.value: Show HN: No more code reviews. Fuzz instead

story_text.value:
My recipe app picked up users when a similar app shut down, and I kept noticing people scrambling to export their data, so I created this project to scratch my own itch.

The 3 main purposes this serves are:

1. Give the public a way to find how to export their data or find a replacement if one of the apps they use shuts down.

2. Give app creators a way to get their apps in front of people who are actively looking for a replacement for a similar app. Sponsored spots are labeled and never change the dates or export steps.

3. Provide inspiration for app creators looking for ideas for what to build next. Just because apps shut down doesn't mean they were not good ideas; many times they shut down for other reasons, like poor execution, no marketing, over-spending, etc.

Every date and export step links to the company's own notice.

I'm always open to ideas to make it more useful. I read all the comments and constructive criticism and input are always welcomed.

title.value: Show HN: Shutdown Watch – App shutdowns, export deadlines, and alternatives

I've been beavering away at this since July, and its finally getting to a point where its stabilising.

It started Windows only, but I recently converted over to Linux, so I've been ironing out the kinks in the last week. You can install it via apt or rpm, or .exe or .msi on Windows.

Many more features to come, including native agent support and more preview features (images, PDF, document formats). Claude works pretty well in it, but I've not tried many other agents yet.

I rarely leave throng now - 99% of my work happens inside it. I stopped using Visual Studio around 10 months ago (in favour of VSCode), and now I don't even use VSCode.

story_text.value:
I am pretty honest: there are a ton of vibecoded projects around, and I made another one... great huh?

I'm working as a data platform engineer in Germany. My day job is basically spinning up & running lakehouse platforms on US hyperscalers for SMB and some DAX companies. I mean, data engineers like to work on these platforms but since some time I really have ethical concerns about it - like: - vendor lock-in - high costs (because of cloud costs - and in most cases you are not able to connect your own metal if you have one) - non-EU vendors... - other open-source solutions have high license costs for LDAP etc. pp.

That's why is started to build my own opinionated data lakehouse platform in my spare time (tbh I also started learning agentic engineering and what harnesses are..), only curated from open source projects already available.

The building blocks are pretty straightforward imo: - Iceberg tables on whatever S3 storage you already have - Trino for SQL and Spark Connect for jobs - Airflow for schedules, plus notebooks, Kafka streams and dashboards - One web UI and one API over all of it - stuff around like OIDC, secrets management etc.

It's fully pre-alpha. But I want to use it as an internal pitch project at my current employer to push agentic engineering & the idea of creating our own data platform for our non-hyperscaler customers.

Site: https://stardelt.io Code: https://github.com/stardelt

I'm happy to hear what you think about it :)

Cheers, Martin

story_text.value:
ScrivenSpell is a word game with RPG elements. If you like Scrabble, you might like this.

This game is inspired by Up Spell, an old iOS game. That game was a lot of fun but unfortunately no longer fits the screen shapes of recent devices.

It also lacked staying power, at least for me, which is why I experimented with RPG elements in ScrivenSpell. With monsters and Quote Quest the player has a series of goals and can work toward 100% completion.

story_text.value:
I am not sure how many here have tried Duolingo for French, but I actually had a hard time speaking in the real world. For me, it is definitely a huge issue. I have level 60, travelled to Paris, and couldn't speak except a few words.

I am Georgian, and nobody taught me how to speak English. I only learned it by watching Game of Thrones multiple times, just using English subtitles and audio for many years, switching between Georgian and English. Watching the same episodes again really helped.

Dual subtitles are what I really needed.

So right now, I am using Netflix and watching my favorite TV show using French audio and French subtitles + English, where I remember most of the dialogues, and I highly recommend everyone to do it! I tried the LanguageReactor Chrome extension, but it wasn't good enough. So I decided to build a new one to actually help me roleplay scenes and practice my speaking, not just save some words. Link in the comments

title.value: Show HN: Learn Languages with Dual Subtitles
